paper.title_en: Equivalent noise charge characterization and operating-point optimization of silicon microstrip modules for the CBM Silicon Tracking System
paper.abstract_en: The Silicon Tracking System (STS) of the Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment at FAIR is designed for charged-particle tracking in a free-streaming, high-rate heavy-ion environment with large occupancies and stringent material-budget requirements. The STS detector modules employ double-sided, double-metal silicon microstrip sensors connected through ultra-light aluminium–polyimide microcables to self-triggering SMX2.2 front-end ASICs. This work presents an experimental characterization of the equivalent noise charge (ENC) performance of STS modules, with emphasis on the dependence of the measured noise response on global register settings that control the buffer and cascode currents of the charge-sensitive amplifier. Pulse-scan measurements were performed for several register configurations using a <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e299"><mrow><mn>6.2</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>12.4</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> sensor module, and the response was analysed separately for the n-side and p-side through channel-by-channel ENC distributions. During operation of some fully assembled detector modules with the initially recommended register settings, non-physical structures were observed in the measured per-channel ENC values on the p-side. This observation motivated a systematic investigation of the ENC performance as a function of the register setting Reg(130,14). The observed dependence is consistent with a reduced phase margin of the charge-sensitive amplifier for certain cascode-current configurations when it is loaded by the module interconnection capacitance, which can introduce oscillatory distortions into the threshold-scan response. Among the tested configurations, an operating point was identified that yields stable amplifier operation without observable oscillatory structures, while simultaneously reducing both the mean apparent ENC and its channel-to-channel spread. The corresponding ADC gain remains within about 5% of the reference setting, demonstrating that stable low-noise operation can be achieved without loss of signal response. This study provides an experimentally motivated choice of front-end operating parameters for STS module qualification and large-scale system integration.
